title: Stomach ultrasound for a vomiting baby (pyloric stenosis)
what: This ultrasound shows the outlet of your baby's stomach: whether it is too narrow and whether milk passes through.
why: Usually for babies in the first weeks of life, when they throw up hard, in a forceful stream, after every feeding.
duration: usually 10 to 20 minutes; the result is given right away
tell_doctor: How many weeks old your baby is
How often and how hard the baby throws up, and if it shoots out
If the baby is gaining weight, and how many wet diapers a day
If there is yellow or green color in the vomit

prepare.title: Feeding
prepare.text: Sometimes you are asked not to feed your baby for 2 to 3 hours. Sometimes the baby is given a drink during the scan. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: For your baby
prepare.text: Bring a bottle, or be ready to breastfeed, if the doctor asks.

bring: A bottle of breast milk or formula
steps: Your baby is laid on their back on the exam table, and you stay close
The doctor puts warm gel on the tummy
The probe is used to look at the stomach and its outlet
Sometimes the baby is given a drink to see how the milk passes
The gel is wiped off, and you are told the result
feel: It does not hurt your baby
The baby may cry from being held or from hunger. That is normal
after: You are told the result right away
If the outlet is narrow, your baby will be referred to a surgeon. It can be treated
Write down feedings and vomiting until you see the doctor
red_flags: Yellow or green vomit: see a doctor right away
The baby is floppy, pees little, or has dry lips: call emergency services
Vomiting after every feeding and the baby is losing weight

faq.q: How do I tell normal spit-up from a dangerous one?
faq.a: Normal spit-up is small, the baby is calm and gaining weight. Forceful vomiting after every feeding and weight loss mean you should see a doctor urgently.

faq.q: If narrowing is found, what happens next?
faq.a: Usually a small operation is planned. A surgeon makes the decision.

reminders.text: Your baby's tummy ultrasound is soon. Bring a bottle, a blanket, and a diaper. Feed as the clinic told you.
